items.title: Put health in the treaty”: youth delegates at the Global Model WHO 2026 adopt declaration on plastics and health
items.summary: This week at WHO headquarters in Geneva, more than 400 young leaders from over 50 countries and all six WHO regions called on governments to protect human health from the preventable harms of plastics.

items.title: Member States reiterate commitment to finalize Pandemic Agreement PABS Annex by May 2027
items.summary: Member States advanced negotiations on the Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) Annex to the WHO Pandemic Agreement, reaffirming their commitment to finalizing the Annex for its consideration by the World Health Assembly in May 2027. The PABS Annex would establish a system that ensures the rapid, transparent sharing of pathogens with pandemic potential and their genetic sequence data, while ensuring rapid and equitable access to the resulting products, including vaccines, diagnostics and t

items.title: Statement of the Forty-sixth Meeting of the Polio IHR Emergency Committee
items.summary: The 46th meeting of the Emergency Committee under the International Health Regulations (IHR or Regulations) on the international spread of poliovirus was convened by the WHO Director-General on 30 September 2026 via video conference with affected countries, supported by the WHO Secretariat.

items.title: Conflict and disease outbreaks deepen DR Congo’s hunger crisis as record numbers are projected to face acute food insecurity
items.summary: FAO, WFP, UNICEF and WHO call for urgent action as acute hunger is projected to hit more than 30 million, including 4.2 million people facing Emergency levels of hunger in early 2027.

items.title: Amid challenges, countries increase domestic investment to protect progress against tuberculosis
items.summary: Global efforts to end tuberculosis (TB) continue to make progress, with fewer people falling ill and dying from the disease, according to the World Health Organization (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 released today.

items.title: Bangladesh and India ban toxic pesticide to boost suicide prevention and brain health
items.summary: Regulatory action on an acutely toxic pesticide will save thousands of lives and protect brain health worldwideGlobally it is estimated 1 in 5 suicides are attributable to the ingestion of acutely toxic pesticides. Many of these deaths are easily preventable and occur in rural communities across Africa, Asia, Eastern Mediterranean, Latin America and the Caribbean, and the Pacific Islands. items.title: WHO and African Medicines Agency advance regulatory cooperation at inaugural Agency Week in Kigali
items.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening Africa's regulatory systems during the inaugural African Medicines Agency (AMA) Week and the 11th African Medicines Regulators Conference (AMRC), held from 25 to 30 October 2026 in Kigali, Rwanda. items.title: WHO launches “Together for Science and Health” movement to strengthen trust worldwide
items.summary: WHO today launched Together for Science and Health, a new global movement uniting more than 240 organizations behind a shared commitment to strengthen trust in science and harness its power to improve health and development.

items.title: From commitments to implementation: ATACH Day at COP31 delivers practical solutions for climate and health
items.summary: This year's ATACH Day, themed “From commitments to implementation: Country solutions for climate and health,” aimed to provide further space to countries showcasing the positive solutions they are implementing in their respective countries.

items.title: WHO updates global catalogue for interpreting tuberculosis drug resistance mutations
items.summary: WHO published the third edition of the Catalogue of mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex and their association with drug resistance, providing the most comprehensive global reference to date for interpreting genomic mutations associated with drug-resistant tuberculosis.

items.title: WHO training strengthens global capacity for healthier, more equitable cities
items.summary: More than half of the world’s population now lives in urban areas, a proportion expected to reach 68% by 2050. While cities can create powerful opportunities for better health, climate action and social development, rapid urbanization is also exposing billions of people to inadequate housing and transport, poor sanitation, air pollution, extreme heat and environments that contribute to noncommunicable diseases and injuries. items.title: WHO releases global mega-map on age-friendly environments
items.summary: The environments in which people live, including their homes, neighbourhoods, transport services and opportunities to participate in community life, play a critical role in healthy ageing. Evidence on how to create age-friendly environments is spread across public health, social care, housing, transport, urban planning and community development, making it difficult for policy-makers and practitioners to see what has been studied and where gaps remain.

items.title: New WHO policy options call for stronger integration of health and care workforce
items.summary: The WHO Academy has launched new policy options to help countries better recognize, develop and support care workers as an integral part of the health workforce, responding to the growing demand for care worldwide as populations age and increasing numbers of people require support due to disability, chronic health conditions and other care needs. items.summary: Consultation period: 8 November 2026 to 6 December 2026Physical inactivity and sedentary behaviour are major risk factors for noncommunicable diseases and poor mental health. Advances in wearable technologies provide an opportunity to complement existing surveillance approaches with objective measures of movement behaviours. items.title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya and Nigeria
items.summary: Since the publication of the previous Disease Outbreak News on 23 October 2026, the Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak has expanded geographically in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. While some areas have seen a slight decline in cases, sustained, high-level transmission continues overall in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. items.title: Civil society discusses its role in strengthening trust in science
items.summary: The WHO Civil Society Commission and WHO Science Department brought together non-State actors to explore how civil society can help strengthen trust in science, counter health misinformation and support the use of evidence. Participants emphasized community engagement, inclusive research, trusted communication and stronger partnerships as key to bringing science closer to people and informing health decisions.

items.title: Yellow fever - WHO African Region
items.summary: Yellow fever transmission continues in the WHO African Region, with recent outbreak activity concentrated in parts of West Africa. Between 1 January and 12 October 2026, 67 confirmed cases, including 18 deaths, were recorded in nine countries in the Region: Burkina Faso, Cameroon, the Central African Republic, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia, Nigeria and Togo. items.title: Shamonda virus in human - France
items.summary: On 20 October 2026, the National IHR Focal Point (NFP) of France notified WHO regarding the first documented human infection with Shamonda virus (SHAV). The case was an immunocompromised older man from eastern France with no travel history during the preceding year. He developed severe neurological illness on 23 September 2026 and was diagnosed with severe encephalitis (brain inflammation). The patient died on 8 October 2026. items.title: Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus - Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
items.summary: Between 1 January and 5 October 2026, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia reported eight laboratory-confirmed cases of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS-CoV) infection, including one death. Cases were detected across six locations: Al Jouf (1), Arar (1), Hafr Al-Batin (1), Riyadh (2), Tabuk (1) and Taif (2). No epidemiological links were identified between any of the cases. items.title: Pneumonia of undetermined etiology - the Russian Federation
items.summary: On 2 October 2026, WHO became aware through media reports of the death of an employee of the Irkutsk Antiplague Research Institute (APRI) of Siberia and the Far East, the Russian Federation. According to these reports, the individual died on 2 October following hospitalization for severe pneumonia on 29 September, and pneumonic plague was suspected as the cause of death, following occupational exposure in laboratory settings. items.title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus - Democratic Republic of the Congo
items.summary: On 5 October 2026, WHO was informed about a laboratory-confirmed imported case of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) in Kenya with travel history from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The patient travelled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to Kenya through Uganda. The patient was hospitalized and treated in Kenya but subsequently died on 5 October. items.summary: Since the last Disease Outbreak News was published on 11 September 2026, the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has expanded further, with two additional health zones affected. These include Bulu health zone in a new province, Sud Ubangi, located on the north-west part of the country and Dungu health zone in Haut-Uélé province, bordering South Sudan. items.summary: Since the last Disease Outbreak News was published on 28 August 2026, the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has expanded to one additional health zone, Kayna, in North Kivu. items.title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus - Democratic Republic of the Congo
items.summary: Since the last Disease Outbreak News was published on 14 August 2026, the outbreak has spread from 54 to 60 health zones. The number of affected provinces stands at six out of 26 provinces of the country: Bas-Uélé, Haut-Uélé, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, and Tshopo. Six additional health zones reported cases since the last update - Ganga and Viadana health zones in Bas-Uélé province, Biena, Manguredjipa, and Mutwanga in North Kivu, and Tshopo health zone in Tshopo province.
